subtopic: Buoyancy, Archimedes' Principle and Relative Density
stem:
Consider the following figures 1 and 2. In figure 1, the mass of the body A in air is 0.2 kg. The mass of the water container (with water in it) is 0.5 kg. In figure 2, when A is completely immersed in the water of the container B, the readings of the respective balances change as shown.

(The figure shows two setups. Figure 1: body A hangs from a spring balance reading 0.2 kg in air, while a beaker of water rests on a separate balance reading 0.5 kg. Figure 2: body A is now fully immersed in the water of beaker B; the spring balance reading falls to 0.15 kg and the beaker balance now reads X kg.)

What is the value of X?

Which of the following graphs shows an approximate variation of g with height h above the Earth's surface?

(The four options are graphs of g on the vertical axis against height h on the horizontal axis. Option a: g starts at the surface value gₑ at h = 0 and decreases along a falling curve as h increases. Option b: g rises from zero up to gₑ along an increasing curve as h increases. Option c: g rises linearly to gₑ at h = 0 only for negative h. Option d: g rises linearly from zero and then stays constant at gₑ.)

options.label: A
options.text: Graph a (g is maximum at the surface and decreases as height h increases)

options.label: B
options.text: Graph b (g increases with height up to gₑ)

stem:
Suppose the acceleration due to gravity at the Earth's surface is 10 m s⁻² and at the surface of Mars is 4 m s⁻². A 60 kg passenger goes from the Earth to the Mars in a spaceship moving with a constant velocity. Neglect all other objects in the sky. Which part of the figure best represents the weight (net gravitational force) of the passenger as a function of time?

(The figure is a graph of Weight (vertical axis, marked 600 N and 200 N) against Time, with the Mars-arrival time marked t₀. Four curves P, Q, R and S all start at 600 N at t = 0. Curve P dips only slightly and ends near 200 N; curve Q dips to a positive minimum and rises back to about 240 N at t₀; curve R dips down to touch zero at t₀; curve S dips below the axis to negative values before returning.)
